title: Geometric Action Model: One Backbone for Geometry and Action
hook: GAM turns a pretrained 3D-geometry model into a robot's brain - a single backbone that forecasts both future geometry and the actions to get there, beating heavier VLA baselines.
key_points: Most vision-language-action models reason over 2D frames or 2D-derived latents, leaving the explicit 3D geometry needed for contact-rich manipulation implicit.
GAM repurposes a pretrained geometric foundation model (GFM) as one shared substrate for perception, temporal prediction, and action decoding.
It splits the GFM mid-stack: early layers encode observations; a causal future predictor forecasts future latent tokens from language, proprioception, and action history.
Predicted tokens flow through the remaining GFM blocks to output both future geometry and actions — one backbone, minimal architectural change.
Across simulation and real-robot manipulation, GAM is reported more accurate, robust, faster, and lighter than foundation-model-scale baselines.
content_html: Generalist robot policies have to follow instructions while reasoning about how objects, cameras, and their own actions interact in 3D space. Recent vision-language-action models (VLAs) and video world-action models inherit strong semantic and temporal priors from foundation models — but they mostly work on 2D image frames or 2D-derived latents, leaving the 3D geometry that contact-rich manipulation needs only implicit.
extra_html: The Geometric Action Model (GAM) takes a different substrate: a pretrained geometric foundation model (GFM), repurposed as a single backbone for perception, temporal prediction, and action decoding. GAM splits the GFM at an intermediate layer — the shallow layers act as an observation encoder, and a causal future predictor inserted at the split forecasts future latent tokens conditioned on language, proprioception, and action history. Those predicted tokens are routed through the remaining GFM blocks, so one network produces both future geometry and the actions to reach it, with minimal architectural change and the GFM's geometric priors preserved. Across a broad suite of simulation and real-robot manipulation benchmarks, the authors report GAM is more accurate, robust, faster, and lighter than current foundation-model-scale baselines.

related.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Model
related.hook: π0 is a generalist robot policy: it takes camera images, joint angles, and a plain-language instruction, and outputs smooth action sequences — folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries.

related.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models
related.hook: Treat a robot's actions as just more text tokens, and a vision-language model can learn to act — carrying its web knowledge into the physical world.

related.title: DreamerV3: Mastering Domains through World Models
related.hook: Instead of learning only from real experience, DreamerV3 builds a world model and practices inside its own imagination — one fixed config, 150+ tasks.

related.title: SeededGrasp: Language-Guided Grasping in Complex Scenes with Multiple Embodiments
related.hook: Instead of one giant end-to-end model, let the VLM just point — predict a seed point, then hand off to a lightweight grasp generator. Data-efficient, and it transfers across robot hands.

flashcards.back_html: They operate on 2D image frames or 2D-derived latents, leaving the explicit 3D geometry needed for contact-rich manipulation implicit.

flashcards.prompt: How does GAM reuse a pretrained geometric foundation model (GFM)?

choices.text: It splits the GFM mid-stack: early layers encode observations, a causal predictor forecasts future latent tokens, later layers decode geometry and actions
It fine-tunes a separate vision encoder and action head from scratch
It distills the GFM into a small 2D convolutional network

flashcards.explanation_html: GAM keeps the GFM's geometric priors by inserting a causal future predictor at an intermediate split, so one backbone serves perception, temporal prediction, and action.

flashcards.prompt: What does GAM's single backbone output, and how does it compare to baselines?
flashcards.back_html: Both future geometry and robot actions. Across simulation and real-robot benchmarks it's reported more accurate, robust, faster, and lighter than foundation-model-scale baselines.
